chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from his father, from Ishaq ibn Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who entered Mecca performing Hajj al-Mufrad and feared that the two standings (at Arafat and Muzdalifah) would be missed. He said to him: 'Your day lasts until the sunrise of the Day of Nahr (Eid al-Adha). When the sun rises, his Hajj is complete.' I asked him: 'What should he do with his Ihram?' He said: 'He should go to Mecca and perform Tawaf around the House and Sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwah.' I asked him: 'When he does that, what does he do afterwards?' He said: 'If he wishes, he stays in Mecca; and if he wishes, he returns to the people in Mina and is not among them in any way; and if he wishes, he returns to his family, and Hajj is incumbent upon him next year.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ihram: The sacred state of consecration entered by pilgrims.
key_terms.الْمَوْقِفَانِ: Al-Mawqifan: The two essential standings at Arafat and Muzdalifah.
key_terms.حَجّ مُفْرَد: Hajj al-Mufrad: A form of pilgrimage where the pilgrim enters Ihram for Hajj only, without combining it with Umrah.
key_terms.سَعْي: Sa'i: The ritual walking between the hills of Safa and Marwah.
key_terms.طُوف: Tawaf: The ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba.
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina: A valley and campsite near Mecca used during Hajj.
key_terms.يَوْمِ النَّحْرِ: Yawm al-Nahr: The Day of Sacrifice, i.e., Eid al-Adha (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who misses the two standings during Hajj al-Mufrad?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s al-Ishtibār clarifies the ruling for a Mufrid pilgrim who misses the critical standing at Arafah until after sunrise on Eid al-Adha, establishing that his Hajj remains valid but incomplete until he performs Tawaf and Sa'i. The Imam’s guidance highlights the flexibility in post-ritual conduct, allowing the pilgrim to either remain in Mecca, return to the crowd in Mina, or depart, while noting that the Hajj obligation is not discharged until these acts are completed. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the validity of the core pillars even if delayed, distinguishing it from the Hanafi view which might consider it a minor Hajj.
